vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle provides standard functionality for replying to Gmail messages via a 'gws' CLI tool. The documentation in SKILL.md describes expected parameters such as message IDs, body text, attachments, and recipient fields (CC/BCC) without any evidence of malicious instructions, prompt injection, or unauthorized data access.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper around the gws CLI for replying to Gmail messages; its declared requirements and actions are consistent, but it defers auth and global flags to a sibling shared file that you should inspect before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (Gws Gmail Reply) matches the declared binary dependency (gws) and the SKILL.md only instructs use of the gws CLI to send replies, which is proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to calling 'gws gmail +reply' with arguments. However the file explicitly tells the agent to read '../gws-shared/SKILL.md' for auth, global flags, and security rules (and to run 'gws generate-skills' if missing). That external-file dependency is out-of-band for this skill and should be inspected because it controls authentication details and any additional behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present (instruction-only). Nothing is written to disk by the skill itself; the only runtime action is invoking the existing gws binary, which is low-risk from an install perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, but it defers auth to '../gws-shared/SKILL.md' and the gws CLI. That means required credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, config files) are hidden from this skill's manifest. Verify what gws and gws-shared require and where they store tokens before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable; it does not request agent-wide persistence or modification of other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not unusual for a CLI wrapper.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill itself is just documentation telling the agent to call the installed gws CLI to reply to Gmail messages, which is consistent with its name. Before installing or enabling it, do the following: (1) Inspect the referenced '../gws-shared/SKILL.md' to see how authentication is handled and what credentials/config files are required; (2) Confirm you trust the gws binary (where it came from and how it stores tokens); (3) Be aware that the gws command will access any files you pass to --attach, and that running 'gws generate-skills' may create files on disk — review what it generates; (4) If you need a tighter manifest, ask the skill author to declare the exact auth requirements rather than deferring to an external file.
